% ============================================================
% Abbeville K-9 Academy grid puzzle - ASP (clingo) encoding
% ============================================================

% ---- Domains ----
months(march;april;may;june).
dogs(aries;barca;hercules;jaws).
officers(daugherty;lyons;quinn;salinas).

% "1 month before" relation over the timeline
order(march,april).
order(april,may).
order(may,june).

% ---- Assignment: each month gets exactly one dog, and vice versa ----
1 { dog(M,D) : dogs(D) } 1 :- months(M).
1 { dog(M,D) : months(M) } 1 :- dogs(D).

% ---- Assignment: each month gets exactly one officer, and vice versa ----
1 { officer(M,O) : officers(O) } 1 :- months(M).
1 { officer(M,O) : months(M) } 1 :- officers(O).

% ============================================================
% Clues
% ============================================================

% Clue 1: The dog that graduated in May was assigned to
%         Officer Salinas or Officer Quinn.
:- officer(may,O), O != salinas, O != quinn.

% Clue 2: Barca graduated in April.
:- dog(april,D), D != barca.

% Clue 3: Officer Lyons's dog graduated exactly 1 month
%         before Officer Daugherty's dog.
:- officer(M1,lyons), officer(M2,daugherty), not order(M1,M2).

% Clue 4: Lyons's dog, the June dog, Jaws, and the April dog
%         are four DIFFERENT dogs (pairwise distinct):
%   - Lyons's dog is not the June dog
:- officer(june,lyons).
%   - Lyons's dog is not the April dog
:- officer(april,lyons).
%   - Jaws is not the June dog
:- dog(june,jaws).
%   - Jaws is not the April dog (also follows from clue 2)
:- dog(april,jaws).
%   - Lyons's dog is not Jaws
:- officer(M,lyons), dog(M,jaws).

% Clue 5: Officer Salinas's dog was Hercules or Barca.
:- officer(M,salinas), dog(M,D), D != hercules, D != barca.

% ============================================================
% Output
% ============================================================
#show dog/2.
#show officer/2.

% ---- Domains ----

winners(charles;freddie;shelley;vicky).
spiders(arachnido;cart_spider;darkback;whip_spider).

1 { winner(P,W) : prices(P) } 1 :- winners(W).

1 { spider(P,S) : spiders(S) } 1 :- prices(P).
1 { spider(P,S) : prices(P) } 1 :- spiders(S).

% ============================================================
% Clues
% ============================================================

% Clue 1: Freddie's purchase cost 15 dollars more than the cart spider.
:- winner(45,W), W != freddie, W != vicky; winner(60,F), F == freddie, not winner(45,W), not winner(60,F).

% Clue 2: Of the darkback and the cart spider, one sold for $60 and the other was won by Vicky.
:- spider(60,D), D != darkback; spider(60,C), C == cart_spider; winner(60,V), V != vicky.

% Clue 3: Of the spider that sold for $75 and Shelley's purchase, one was the archaenido and the other was the cart spider.
:- spider(75,A), A != arachnido; winner(75,S), S != shelley; winner(45,W), W == shelley, not spider(45,S); spider(45,S), S == arachnido, not winner(45,W).

% Clue 4: The arachnid that sold for $90 was either Shelley's purchase or the darkback.
:- spider(90,A), A != arachnido; winner(90,S), S != shelley; spider(60,D), D == darkback, not spider(90,D); winner(60,V), V == vicky, not spider(60,V).

% Riverside Vintage Watch Exchange grid puzzle - ASP (clingo) encoding
% ============================================================

% ---- Domains ----
prices(300;350;400;475).
brands(bulova;citizen;hamilton;seiko).
face_colors(blue;green;red;silver).

% ---- Assignment: each price gets exactly one brand and face color, and vice versa ----
1 { brand(P,B) : brands(B) } 1 :- prices(P).
1 { face_color(P,F) : face_colors(F) } 1 :- prices(P).

% ---- Each price has a unique combination of brand and face color ----
:- brand(P,B1), brand(P,B2), B1 != B2.
:- face_color(P,F1), face_color(P,F2), F1 != F2.

% ============================================================
% Clues
% ============================================================

% Clue 1: The Tissot watch was either the timepiece with a silver face or the one with a blue dial.
% Note: Tissot is not in brands, so this must be inferred through brand and face color constraints.
:- brand(P,tissot), face_color(P,green), face_color(P,red).

% Clue 2: The watch with a blue dial sold for 75 dollars less than the Bulova model.
:- face_color(P1,blue), brand(P2,bulova), P2 = P1 + 75.

% Clue 3: Of the $400 watch and the $350 piece, one is a Hamilton model and the other has a green face.
:- brand(400,hamilton), face_color(350,green).
:- brand(350,hamilton), face_color(400,green).

% Clue 4: The Seiko model sold for somewhat more than the Citizen model.
:- brand(P1,seiko), brand(P2,citizen), P1 > P2.

% Clue 5: The watch with a silver face sold for 125 dollars more than the timepiece with a green face.
:- face_color(P1,silver), face_color(P2,green), P1 = P2 + 125.

% ============================================================
% Output
% ============================================================
#show brand/2.
#show face_color/2.
